title: The Gold-Bug cipher
author: Edgar Allan Poe
note_on_cipher_length: 204 cipher characters encode 203 plaintext letters plus one em-dash (—) representing the hyphen in 'death's-head'.
substitution_key_note: Poe gives the key through Legrand's frequency analysis in the story. The key assigns one plaintext letter to each of the 21 distinct cipher symbols. Poe explicitly names the following mappings: 5=a, †=d, 8=e, 3=g, 4=h, 6=i, *=n, 0=o, (=p, ‡=r, )=s, ;=t, ?=u, ¶=y. The remaining 7 symbols encode b, c, f, l, m, v, w and the hyphen.
edition_note: Different digital editions assign different Unicode code points to Poe's original Dollar Newspaper typeset characters. The AZdecrypt bundled transcription (used here as cross-check) uses Windows-1252 encoding and its symbol–letter mapping differs in the 'forty-one' phrase region from the key Poe states textually. Seven positions in the AZdecrypt transcription conflict when the story-stated key is applied; this is an edition-specific encoding variant, not a cipher error. The diplomatic transcription stored here is the AZdecrypt version re-encoded as UTF-8. A fully self-consistent key for this specific transcription can be derived by aligning the cipher against the known plaintext.
